title: Energy-efficient QRS detection on ultra-low-power microcontrollers for long-term cardiac patches

record.title: Energy-efficient QRS detection on ultra-low-power microcontrollers for long-term cardiac patches
record.abstract: Battery life is the dominant constraint for wearable cardiac patches intended for multi-week arrhythmia screening. This paper presents an ultra-low-power QRS detection algorithm specifically designed for deployment on a 16-bit microcontroller operating at 8 MHz with 4 kB of available SRAM. The algorithm adapts the classical Pan–Tompkins pipeline by replacing floating-point operations with integer arithmetic and replacing the bandpass filter with a computationally cheaper differentiator-squarer cascade whose coefficients are pre-quantized to powers of two, enabling shift-based multiplication. Threshold adaptation is reformulated as a recursive integer update requiring no division. The implementation is benchmarked on five publicly available ECG databases totalling over 120,000 annotated beats, achieving a detection sensitivity of 99.1% and positive predictivity of 98.9%. On the target microcontroller, the algorithm consumes 87 μW at 500 Hz input, extending projected patch lifetime from 9 to 21 days compared with a floating-point baseline at equivalent sampling rate. The source code is released openly to support reproducibility and adoption in resource-constrained medical device development.
